content: Oral contraceptives are pharmaceutical agents administered orally with the primary purpose of preventing pregnancy. For females, there are two main types of oral contraceptive pills that are widely available: 1. The combined oral contraceptive pill contains two active hormonal components: estrogen and a progestogen. This pill is designed to be taken once daily. 2. The progestogen-only pill, often referred to as the mini-pill, contains only a progestogen as its active ingredient. Like the combined pill, it is also taken once daily. In addition to these widely used options, there are other types of female oral contraceptives that are either experimental or available only in specific regions: Mifepristone, an antiprogestogen, has been investigated as a daily oral contraceptive in clinical trials, though it is not widely approved for this purpose. Ormeloxifene, also known as Centchroman, is a selective estrogen receptor modulator. It is taken less frequently, typically one to two times per week. Currently, Ormeloxifene is approved for use as an oral contraceptive only in India. For males, there are no oral contraceptives currently available on the market. However, several potential male oral contraceptive options are under active research and development.
